title: Digital Gatekeeping: An Audit of Search Engine Results shows tailoring of queries on the Israel-Palestine Conflict
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the political leaning (pro-Israel vs. pro-Palestine) of search engine results for queries related to the Israel-Palestine conflict. This indirectly assesses how user context, including locations with distinct majority religious populations (Jewish, Muslim, Christian), affects the presentation of a religio-political conflict. The study also included specific queries about religious sites, such as Orthodox churches in Gaza.
findings: The study found significant customization of search results concerning the Israel-Palestine conflict based on user location, language, and browsing history. This tailoring extends to the political leaning of the content. Bots in locations with different majority religious demographics (e.g., Israel - Jewish, Saudi Arabia - Muslim, Brazil - Christian) received different search results. The findings indicate that DuckDuckGo and Google tend to show more pro-Israel content in their top 3 results, with the proportion of pro-Palestine content decreasing depending on the bot's location.
